metadata.title: Transform Your PWA to a Native App with Capacitor
metadata.description: Convert an existing Progressive Web App into a native Capacitor mobile app for iOS and Android. A practical guide to packaging your PWA with minimal code changes.
metadata.author: Martin Donadieu
metadata.head_image_alt: Transform Your PWA to a Native App with Capacitor Capgo blog illustration
metadata.keywords: PWA, Capacitor, native mobile app, iOS, Android, web-to-app migration, web app deployment

blocks.text: You already have a Progressive Web App. It works in browsers, has a manifest, and maybe uses a service worker for offline support. If you now need app store distribution, native device APIs, or a better onboarding funnel, migrating to a Capacitor app is usually faster than rewriting your front end.
The biggest advantage is that you keep almost all of your existing web code. In most cases, you only need to:
and wire native plugins only where needed.
If your PWA has clean routes and component logic, this can take just a few hours.

Remove hard-coded absolute redirects that assume browser-only context.
Verify service worker behavior is compatible with mobile WebViews:
Keep offline support if it helps your users.
Avoid browser-only APIs that are unavailable in the embedded webview.
Confirm PWA install prompts and browser-specific UX still make sense. In a Capacitor app, app install prompts are usually not needed.
Keep your app UI but gate browser-only logic.
Use a simple platform check around install and push prompts:
This avoids browser-only logic firing inside the native container.
Step 3: Initialize Capacitor in your PWA folder
Run Capacitor init with your app name, bundle ID, and web output directory:
bunx cap init MyPWAApp com.example.my-pwa-app --web-dir dist
Install core native packages and generate project folders:

bun add @capacitor/ios @capacitor/android
bunx cap add ios
bunx cap add android
At this point Capacitor has created
folders. Syncing will copy your built web assets into both platforms.
Step 5: Build your web app and sync
Build the PWA and sync web assets:

bun run build
bunx cap sync

bunx cap open ios
bunx cap open android
From Xcode or Android Studio, connect a device or emulator and run.

You already did most of the hard work when building your PWA. Wrapping it with Capacitor gives you:
Faster iteration without a full code rewrite,
A single deployment path for web and mobile teams.
Start from this flow, then iterate native-by-native based on analytics and user feedback.
